summary: John Wayne Airport operates under a settlement agreement, extended in 2014 through 31 December 2030, that caps annual passengers: 11.8 million a year for 2021 to 2025, then 12.2 or 12.5 million a year for 2026 to 2030 depending on service levels. Traffic cannot grow past the cap whatever the demand.
The same agreement also restricts departures, operating hours (a night curfew) and passenger loading bridges; the County's curfew obligation runs through 2035.
SFO's two parallel runways are about 750 feet apart. In late March 2026 the FAA ended side-by-side landings on them, cutting the arrival rate from about 54 to 36 per hour.

From 12 August 2026 the FAA allowed staggered landings on the parallel runways in good weather, raising the limit to about 42 arrivals per hour; low visibility brings it back down. Runway 1R/19L was closed for repaving, with further relaxation expected after it reopens.
